claims.label: Unattended Items Seized Near Library Bus Stop
claims.claim: Sergeant Filomena testified that officers canvassing the scene seized unattended items — including a backpack, jacket, and gloves — near the Folsom (Fulton) Library bus stop.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain hearing transcript or video exhibits to verify item count (three vs. nine) and chain of custody.

claims.label: UVU Communicated Discontinuation of Testing to FBI
claims.claim: Sergeant Filomena acknowledged that items were sent to the FBI lab and that UVU eventually communicated to the lab that the items were not connected to the case and required no further testing.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain FBI/ATF lab correspondence and UVU communications log for the testing discontinuation instruction.

claims.label: Eyewitness Observed Tactical Movement Pattern on Rooftop
claims.claim: The anonymous eyewitness recorded on September 25 that the rooftop person executed a tactical movement pattern (rising/lowering in 6-foot increments) over approximately 30 seconds before assuming the prone shooting position.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare witness description to rooftop video exhibits and to expert definitions of Individual Movement Technique (IMT).

claims.label: Eyewitness Described All-Black Tactical Attire and Face Mask
claims.claim: The anonymous eyewitness described the rooftop person as wearing all-black tactical gear with a face mask; could not determine race because skin was covered.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference with police scanner descriptions and the 911 call (A-2141.1); obtain witness's filed written report.

claims.label: Eyewitness Described Rifle as Smaller than Mauser, Resembling .223
claims.claim: The eyewitness described the rooftop person's rifle as looking smaller than a .30-06 (and specifically as appearing to be a .223), contradicting the recovered Mauser per the witness.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference with recovered weapon evidence and any unfired .223 round testimony referenced at 26:40.

claims.label: 911 Caller Reported Person on Building Near Library
claims.claim: A 911 caller reported a person on the building on the far north side, just east of the library, wearing jeans, black shirt, black vest, and a black mask, carrying a long rifle.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain full 911 transcript and dispatch records for the library area to verify caller statement and subsequent library lockdown.

claims.label: Police Scanner Reported Face Mask and Tactical Gear
claims.claim: Host states that initial police scanner traffic described a person in a face mask and tactical gear, contrasting with subsequent federal narrative claims of jeans-only attire.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain police scanner audio archive and CAD logs from Sept 10 to verify initial dispatch descriptions.

claims.label: Federal Authorities Contacted Eyewitness Only Once; Not Called by Prosecution
claims.claim: The eyewitness was contacted by federal authorities only once, a few days after the incident, and has never been called as a prosecution witness despite being willing to testify.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain prosecution witness list for Tyler Robinson trial; confirm whether witness was subpoenaed or deposed.

claims.label: Frank Turek Worked as Bank of America Consultant for ~15 Years
claims.claim: Per Christian Post article (2011), Dr. Frank Turek was a consultant to Bank of America for approximately 15 years conducting leadership and team-building programs until being fired in 2011.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify Bank of America consultancy records and corroborate the 2011 firing and stated reason.

claims.label: Nate Walker: Charlie Chose "Freedom Shirt" Because "Not Controversial"
claims.claim: Nate Walker, Charlie's executive assistant, told Megyn Kelly that Charlie requested the "freedom shirt" from a small selection brought to the event because it "wasn't controversial"; Walker could not recall other shirt options.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain full Megyn Kelly interview and any prior on-record statements by Walker.

claims.label: Comperatore Asserts Butler Shooting Was "Inside Job"
claims.claim: Helen Comperatore stated on NewsNation that she believes the Butler shooter Thomas Crooks was working with someone inside the government, describing it as "an inside job."
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain full NewsNation interview; identify any specific evidence references Comperatore cited ("I've been told things").

claims.label: Comperatore: Secret Service Did Not Reach Out for a Year
claims.claim: Per host reporting on NewsNation interview, Helen Comperatore stated that Secret Service did not contact her until a year after the Butler incident and did not fully answer her questions.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain NewsNation transcript and verify Secret Service contact timeline with the Comperatore family.

claims.label: Time Reported Israeli PR Campaign via Clock Tower X Backfired
claims.claim: Time magazine reported that the Brad Parscale / Clock Tower X digital influence campaign on behalf of the Israeli foreign ministry backfired and failed to achieve its intended impact.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain Time article in full; verify spend figures and named individuals (e.g., Eyal Yakoby).

claims.label: Time Reported Campaign Spend of ~$1.5 Million/Day
claims.claim: Per Time article reporting, the Israeli foreign ministry's contracted digital campaign via Clock Tower X was reportedly spending approximately $1.5 million per day.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the $1.5M/day figure against the Time article text and any underlying contracts/filings cited.

claims.label: Charlie Wore Custom Carhartt Shirt on Sept 10, Not Sold "Freedom Shirt"
claims.claim: Host displays a photo showing Charlie Kirk wearing a customized Carhartt shirt (logo visible) on September 10, distinct from the all-cotton "freedom shirts" sold through TPUSA's for-profit arm after the assassination.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the vendor/contractor who produced the custom Carhartt shirt and the authorization chain for the custom order.
